WAS@NYG.text: Round one ended in a tie because Washington ran out of clock in overtime. Meanwhile, the Giants have covered six of eight.

NE@DET.text: The Over is 6-0 in New England's last six games, while the Under is 3-0 in Detroit's last three. One streak dies in Munich.

BUF@NYJ.text: The Jets have allowed 26+ points in four straight losses, and Buffalo is 5-0 against the spread in the last five meetings. Rough neighborhood.

CAR@NO.text: Saints DE Chase Young has eight sacks in eight games, second in the NFL. Panthers linemen, consider yourselves warned.

HOU@CLE.text: The Texans are 0-4 at home but 3-1 on the road. Lucky for them, they're in Cleveland, where the Browns are 3-0.

JAX@TEN.text: Trevor Lawrence threw for 484 yards and five TDs in two games against the Titans last season. The 1-7 Titans remember.

KC@ATL.text: Bijan Robinson leads the NFL with 880 rushing yards, which is about the only thing the 3-6 Falcons are leading.

MIA@IND.text: Daniel Jones has thrown an interception in eight of nine games, including four straight. Dolphins DBs, bring your gloves.

MIN@GB.text: Kyler Murray (hamstring) remains week-to-week, so Kirk Cousins starts at Lambeau. Packers fans know that face.

LA@ARI.text: With Gardner Minshew doubtful, Carson Beck gets his first NFL start. The Rams' Puka Nacua is listed as doubtful.

SEA@LV.text: Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza makes his first NFL start for the Raiders, while Seattle stays without Sam Darnold. Rookie welcome party, Vegas style.

SF@DAL.text: CeeDee Lamb dropped 195 receiving yards last week. Brock Purdy has a TD pass in eight straight. Defense is optional.

PIT@CIN.text: Both teams are 6-2 riding four-game win streaks, with the AFC North lead on the line. Pittsburgh won the first one 30-27.

LAC@BAL.text: The 0-8 Chargers are 0-7-1 against the spread. The Ravens are 2-7 ATS and without Lamar Jackson (IR). Something has to give.

IND@HOU.text: The Texans are 0-4 against the spread at home and just blew a 17-0 lead to Cleveland. Vegas still has them as big favorites.

ARI@KC.text: Carson Beck is out, so 40-year-old Josh Johnson starts for Arizona, his 15th NFL team. Arrowhead awaits.

BAL@CAR.text: Lamar Jackson is out and Jacoby Brissett starts: four different Ravens QBs in four games. Baltimore has lost five straight.

JAX@NYG.text: The Giants haven't beaten Jacksonville at home since 2010. Trevor Lawrence and the 7-2 Jaguars would love to keep that going.

MIA@BUF.text: Kyle McCord is the fourth straight backup QB to face Buffalo, whose defense has allowed 28 points total in its last three games.

NO@CHI.text: The Bears scored 27+ in four straight wins with Caleb Williams, and now Kyle Monangai is back after missing five games. Good luck, Saints.

TB@DET.text: Baker Mayfield (foot) will play against the Lions after a questionable week, per Ian Rapoport. The Bucs' gunslinger is back in the saddle.

TEN@DAL.text: Dallas gave up 584 yards to the 49ers and handed defensive play-calling to Mike Pettine. The Titans have averaged 27.3 points over four games.

NYJ@LAC.text: Geno Smith plans to play through his ankle injury. The Jets offense has gone nine straight quarters without a touchdown, so no pressure.

LV@DEN.text: Fernando Mendoza was sacked six times in his first start. Next up: a Denver defense with 26 sacks and a five-game win streak.

PIT@PHI.text: Joe Milton starts for an Eagles team on a seven-game losing streak. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers roll into the Linc as road favorites.

MIN@SF.text: Minnesota allows a league-low 14 points a game. San Francisco scores TDs on 82.8% of red-zone trips. Something has to give in Mexico City.

CIN@WAS.text: Vegas pushed MVP favorite Joe Burrow and the Bengals from 3.5-point favorites to 6.5, and the total climbed too. Washington, you've been warned.

GB@LA.text: Puka Nacua is out for the season, yet Blake Corum has scored in six straight games and the Rams ride a four-game win streak.

CHI@DET.text: Detroit plays without Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell (both on IR), and the Lions are 38-46-2 all-time on Thanksgiving. Pass the gravy.

PHI@DAL.text: Jalen Hurts is on IR, so Joe Milton starts for an Eagles team that's 2-8 against the spread. Dak has nine TDs in two weeks.

KC@BUF.text: Mahomes and Allen are 5-5 head-to-head, and Patrick Mahomes is 13-4-1 against the spread as an underdog. Turkey-night tiebreaker.

DEN@PIT.text: The Broncos have won 16 straight one-possession games. Steelers, maybe try a different kind of game.

ATL@MIN.text: The under is 9-1 in Vikings games this season. Pack a snack, folks, the scoreboard operator sure is.

BAL@HOU.text: Lamar Jackson is on IR and the Ravens are 3-8 against the spread. Meanwhile, C.J. Stroud has 3+ TD passes in three straight.

NO@CIN.text: Joe Burrow has 29 TD passes and still slipped to No. 2 in MVP odds behind Brock Purdy. The Saints draw a grumpy QB.

NYG@IND.text: Anthony Richardson Sr. makes his first start since 2024 after the Colts cut Daniel Jones. Fresh keys, 6.5-point home dog.

NYJ@MIA.text: With Malik Willis on IR, Kyle McCord is poised to start. Last week he went 12-for-33 for 102 yards. Jets defense, stretch out.

TEN@JAX.text: The Titans have allowed 40-plus points three straight games. Next stop: a Jaguars team favored by 14.5.

NE@LAC.text: Drake Maye is out, so Tommy DeVito starts. The line shrank from 4.5 to 1.5, but the 1-9 Chargers are somehow still favored.

SEA@SF.text: The 9-1 49ers already beat Seattle 32-29 and can sweep. Sam Darnold is questionable. Defending champs, no pressure.

WAS@ARI.text: The Cardinals lost their last two games by a combined 68-13. The Commanders would like a word, and a third straight win.

LV@CLE.text: The Browns are favored by 4.5 but haven't won a game by more than four all season. Math is hard on Sunday night.

CAR@TB.text: The 5-5 Panthers lead the NFC South by two games and are still underdogs to the 3-7 Bucs. Revenge Monday, anyone?
